Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. If I missed anything, please flag.

Pain points you shared:
- Need to add a GenAI assistant to customer support workflows but cannot send raw customer PII to external services.
- Current stack: support messages stored in-house (Postgres + S3), existing internal ML infra is limited; want a managed inference option.
- Need robust audit logs for model input/output for compliance and periodic audits.

Success criteria for an initial pilot:
- Redwood-hosted endpoint that never persists PII in logs or stored payloads for the pilot data set.
- Retention policy: logs kept for 90 days, then auto-deleted unless flagged for audit.
- Redaction: ability to redact or tokenize PII before storage and provide secure audit trail of redaction decisions.
- Throughput/latency target: ~200 reqs/min with 200–500ms median latency for single-turn responses.

Key constraints and questions we captured:
- Which fields you consider PII (you mentioned name, national id, account numbers, and any free-text that could include PII).
- Legal wants an auditable redaction log (who redacted and why) — do you need per-token redaction visibility or just per-request indicators?
- SOC 2 evidence: you requested a copy of our retention, logging, and key management overview.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a filled security questionnaire and a short SOW draft for the pilot (attached).
2) Michael (cc’d) will follow up with an implementation note on redaction options (client-side redaction vs server-side PII scrubbing) and what audit logs look like.
3) Align on exact PII field list and retention window by next Wed (2026-05-27).

Attachments: FinCo_Security_Questionnaire_Completed.xlsx (filled), FinCo_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW for pilot).

Hi Sara / Tom —

Quick technical note on options we discussed:

1) Client-side PII redaction (recommended for lowest log surface):
   - You run a small redaction library before requests leave your environment. Redwood receives already-scrubbed payloads and returns responses.
   - Audit trail: client logs redaction actions locally; Redwood provides request ids and encrypted metadata to link responses to your local audit when needed.
   - Pros: minimal PII exposure to Redwood infra; lowest compliance friction.
   - Cons: requires changes to your pipeline; you retain primary redaction logs.

2) Server-side redaction with per-token audit (Redwood-managed):
   - We can deploy a middleware that marks tokens flagged as PII and store a per-token redaction map in the audit log.
   - Retention & deletion: logs stored encrypted with KMS; retention TTL configurable (we can set 90 days for the pilot).
   - Audit access: logs can be exported to your S3 or accessed via secure one-time URL for audits.
   - Pros: no changes to your upstream; centralizes redaction for review.
   - Cons: increases log surface and may add ~50–150ms request latency depending on tokenization/redaction settings.

Operational controls we can enable for the pilot:
- Redaction policy templates (strict / permissive) you can toggle per environment.
- Auto-delete job that purges logs after TTL; manual retention hold for audit cases.
- Immutable audit trail for who requested redaction toggles and who accessed the logs (access logs).

I’ll attach a short diagram and the security questionnaire answers for what we encrypt at rest/in transit. If FinCo wants per-token redaction for compliance, we can scope it as a pilot feature but will need an SE kickoff to benchmark latency.

Happy to jump on a call next week to walk through a demo of the redaction UI and audit exports.
